findings.minimal_remediation: Document the required SSM tag keys and semantics in instruction or a referenced docs contract, or stop asserting those private keys.
findings.regression_risk: Changing tag vocabulary without updating inherited Terraform/fixtures will break oracle and F2P READY paths.
findings.why_it_matters: Controller add-ons are only recognized when aws_ssm_parameter tags use exact keys ControllerAddon, AddonVersion, and ResolveConflicts; those key names never appear in instruction.md or /app/docs, so a fair solver cannot discover the graded encoding.

findings.minimal_remediation: Publish AddonTrust (and any required companion tags) in the solver-visible IRSA/docs contract, or grade roles via an already-documented identifier.
findings.regression_risk: Retagging roles may invalidate SA annotation ARN pairing tests.
findings.why_it_matters: IRSA discovery, forbidden-subject checks, policy merge, and naming all key off the undocumented AddonTrust tag; without it plan_policy reports missing roles and F2P fails.

findings.minimal_remediation: Document the Terraform/SSM encoding for regulated private on-demand fencing, or derive regulated posture solely from documented Karpenter/workload manifests already graded.
findings.regression_risk: Removing TF-side regulated checks without retaining CRD/workload assertions could weaken placement coverage.
findings.why_it_matters: plan_policy_errors requires graph.regulated.name/capacity_types/private_only populated only from SSM tags RegulatedNodePool/Component, CapacityTypes, PrivateSubnetsOnly, and NodePoolName—none documented in solver-visible contracts—while F2P asserts those graph fields.

findings.minimal_remediation: Assert each required PDB selector matchLabels equals pdbs.json, and/or fail _pdb_coverage on selector mismatch.
findings.regression_risk: Strict selector checks will fail submissions that only fix names/minAvailable.
findings.why_it_matters: Instruction requires PDBs that match pdbs.json, which includes selectors; test_f2p_pdbs_match_required_names_namespaces_selectors and _pdb_coverage only check name/namespace/minAvailable, so wrong selectors still pass.

findings.minimal_remediation: Extend plan_policy_errors and F2P assertions to reject Resource wildcards and service-wildcard actions for every AddonTrust role, aligned with the published rule.
findings.regression_risk: May fail policies that relied on undocumented allowlist wildcards in defaults.json.
findings.why_it_matters: Contracts forbid wildcard IAM Action and Resource (including service wildcards); verifier only bans defaults.forbidden_policy_actions plus ebs_csi actions ending in :*, so Resource=* and non-ebs service:* policies can still READY.

findings.minimal_remediation: Remove wildcard entries from allowed_policy_prefixes or explicitly redefine the no-wildcard rule and enforce one authoritative allowlist.
findings.regression_risk: Clarifying either direction changes which IAM documents pass policy gates.
findings.why_it_matters: defaults.allowed_policy_prefixes lists service wildcards (e.g. elasticloadbalancing:*, ec2:Describe*) while instruction/docs forbid wildcard actions; graders ignore the allowlist, leaving conflicting authorities for accepted IAM shape.

findings.minimal_remediation: Make both docs and digest/schema tests agree on whether role_arn is required in published bindings.
findings.regression_risk: Low if digest subset stays stable.
findings.why_it_matters: report-schema.md requires irsa_bindings.*.role_arn while addon-trust-rollout-contract.md omits it and digest hashing drops role_arn; nested field obligation is unclear though top-level READY checks still pass.

role_output.REMOVAL_TEST: Removing ~25% of solver-visible core (e.g. plan_validator+irsa_verifier, or drain+placement+interruption, or the coordinator state machine) collapses whole readiness classes and report fields. Removing only unused SSM inventory markers would not materially change lab outcomes, confirming residual padding there, but not that the remaining system is toy.
role_output.SUBSTANTIVE_LOC_ASSESSMENT: Approximately 2600 LOC of reachable Python under upgrade_lab/ plus bin/addon-trust-rollout; plus consumed Terraform (workspace + modules/upgrade/main.tf resources the normalizer ingests), k8s manifests loaded by apply_k8s_manifests, and curated data JSON loaded by the coordinator. Combined substantive reachable runtime/config is above ~3000 LOC. Secondary SSM inventory in addons.tf/irsa.tf/nodepools.tf (~250+ LOC) is planned but largely ignored by ingest_ssm_parameter and is not counted as substantive. Docs are context, not logic. Domain state is curated ops fixtures (matrix/trust/snapshot/events), appropriate for a control-plane lab rather than bulk business-record scale.

Q6_RESULT.summary: Solver-visible core is a coherent multi-stage EKS add-on trust upgrade control plane: Terraform plan ingestion, multi-policy validation, IRSA fencing, ordered rollout with checkpoints, PDB/drain simulation, regulated placement, and interruption handling are reachable from the operator entrypoint, materially differentiated, and cross-coupled with distinct failure reasons. Substantive reachable runtime/config exceeds a production floor once unused SSM inventory markers are discounted; toy/padding risk is not HIGH.
